title: Quantifying and Attributing Polarization to Annotator Groups
benchmark_measurement: The paper introduces and applies a metric ('apunim') to measure polarization in annotations for toxicity and hate speech detection. For religion, it specifically measures how the self-reported importance of religion to an annotator contributes to polarization, i.e., whether religious or irreligious annotators disagree more with other groups or amongst themselves.
findings: On toxicity detection tasks, the importance of religion to an annotator shows a monotonic trend with polarization. Very religious annotators tend to agree among themselves but fundamentally disagree with other annotators. Conversely, non-religious (irreligious) annotators are more divided among themselves, exhibiting higher internal polarization. This trend is gradually diminished and then reversed as the reported importance of religion increases.
